dataset.title: Clinical Correlations Logic Seed
dataset.description: Topographic, neurovascular, lesion and surgical-danger correlations designed to sit on top of the Anatomy Structures v2 database.

logic_model.purpose: Allow the app to answer and quiz clinically relevant relation questions, not just list isolated anatomical structures.

query_intents.example: What artery runs along the greater curvature of the stomach?
Which nerve is injured at the neck of fibula?
What happens in CN VI palsy?
What is the order in the femoral triangle?
Why can a posterior duodenal ulcer bleed badly?

answer_contract.short_answer: One direct answer suitable for search preview or quiz answer.
answer_contract.exam_answer: Direct answer plus relation, course/origin, clinical relevance and trap.
answer_contract.provenance: Always expose review status and source_refs. If source_refs are empty, show seed/review warning.

ranking_rules: Exact structure/container match beats broad text match.
Relation type matching the query intent beats generic clinical note match.
Course week context can boost relevant correlations during course study.
If several vessels/structures are correct, return ordered or segmented answer rather than one arbitrary result.

correlations.answer: The greater curvature of the stomach is supplied by an arterial arcade formed mainly by the right gastro-omental artery and the left gastro-omental artery.

arteries.name: right gastro-omental artery
arteries.course: runs from right to left along the greater curvature between layers of the greater omentum

arteries.name: left gastro-omental artery
arteries.course: runs from left to right along the greater curvature

details.contrast: lesser curvature is supplied by right and left gastric arteries

clinical_relevance: Important during gastric surgery and control of bleeding along the greater curvature.
exam_traps: Do not answer right gastric or left gastric artery; those follow the lesser curvature.
Short gastric arteries supply mainly the fundus near the superior part of the greater curvature, not the full inferior greater-curvature arcade.
question_templates: Which arteries run along the greater curvature of the stomach?
Which artery passes along the inferior/great-curvature side of the stomach?
Greater curvature bleeding: which vessels are nearby?

evidence.note: Educational anatomy seed correlation. Requires human/faculty review before being marked verified.

direct_synonyms: which artery passes along stomach greater curvature
negative_traps: Do not answer right gastric or left gastric artery; those follow the lesser curvature.
Short gastric arteries supply mainly the fundus near the superior part of the greater curvature, not the full inferior greater-curvature arcade.

correlations.answer: The lesser curvature is supplied by the right gastric and left gastric arteries, which anastomose along the lesser curvature.
clinical_relevance: Important in gastric ulcer bleeding and gastric mobilization.
exam_traps: Do not confuse with gastro-omental arteries, which follow the greater curvature.

distractor_strategy.vessel_questions: Use vessels from the same region or same organ-system territory.
distractor_strategy.nerve_questions: Use nearby nerves, branches from the same plexus, or common confusion pairs.
distractor_strategy.foramen_questions: Use foramina from the same skull base group.
distractor_strategy.ordered_contents: Shuffle correct contents or use common incorrect order.
